Judgment:

1. By this order I shall dispose of the petition filed on behalf of the petitioners under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act for the unfortunate death of deceased Kavita Gupta @ Kavita Goel who met with an road accident occurred on 22.08.2019 at about 02.05 pm at opposite Sai Hotel G.T.
Road.
She has left behind her husband, three daughters which includes two minor daughters.

2. The facts of this case need not having any big canvas:-
"On 22.08.2019 at about 02.05 pm, the husband of the deceased along with deceased were coming on his motorcycle no. DL-9S-BM-9628 from Kheda Dharampura to Chaprola via G.T. Road.
When they reached Opposite Sai Hotel G.T. road at Ghaziabad, Dadri road, a vehicle no. UP-14-HT-2963 came from behind being driven in a rash and negligent manner had hit their motorcycle.
Resulting to which he fell down and sustained grievous injury.
Neeraj Aggarwal and ors.
Vs Babluy and
ors. 18.01.2023 Page No. 2 of 18 Deceased Kavita was died on the spot."
3. Notice of the petition was issued to the respondents.
4. Written statement has been filed on behalf of the respondent no. 2/ Manoj Kumar who has stated that the petitioner is not maintainable qua the answering respondent.
He submitted that at the time of accident driver Bablu was driving the vehicle bearing UP-14-HT- 2967 in control speed.
He submitted that the vehicle was duly insured.

5. Reply has also been filed on behalf of the insurance company wherein it has stated that the answering respondent denies all the allegations contained in the present petition, save and except to the extent the contents thereof are specifically admitted.
No allegation should be deemed to have been admitted for want of a specific denial.
However, it has admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with it.

6. After completion of pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 17.08.2022, following issues have been framed:-
1.

Whether deceased Kavita Gupta succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road accident on 22.08.2019 at 2.05 pm opposite Sai Hotel G.T. Road due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. UP-14-HT-2963 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent Neeraj Aggarwal and ors.
Vs Babluy and ors.

11.It is well settled law that where petition under Section 166 of the Act is instituted, it becomes the duty of the petitioner to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver.

sentences.text: Basically, in road accident cases, Tribunal has simply to quantify the compensation which is just rational and reasonable on the basis of enquiry.

Though it is an admitted legal position that the negligence on the part of driver with respect to the use of vehicle needs to be established but the same is to be established on the principles of preponderance of probabilities as decided in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Harsh Mishra & Ors. III(2015) ACC 435 Delhi.

sentences.text: In the present case, manner of accident has not been disputed.
PW 1 the husband of the deceased was examined in the witness box, however, nothing substantial has come out from the mouth of the witness which could put dent upon the testimony of the PW 1.

Since, the insurance company has not contested the case about rash and negligent act of driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and the insurance company has no statutory defence, therefore, no further discussion is required in order to prove this issue.
Hence, this issue stands proved in favour of the petitioners and against the respondent.
13. Now, the court has to assess as to how much compensation be awarded to the petitioners and by whom.
First of all the court has to decide as to whom the liability to pay the compensation is fastened.
14.As regards the liability, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, therefore primary liability to compensate the petitioner is that of respondent no.1.
As the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no.2, so, it is vicariously liable to compensate the petitioner.
It is an admitted position on record that the offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident.
Therefore, it is the respondent no. 3 who has to compensate the petitioner being the insurer.
Neeraj Aggarwal and ors.

Now the next question arises as to how much compensation is to be granted to the petitioners.
PW 1, the husband of the deceased has stated that the petitioners are the residents of the Delhi for the last 35-36 years.
However, they have not placed any document on record in regard to their residence in Delhi for such long years.
Accident was occurred at Gautambudh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.
It is a matter of fact that address mentioned on the Election I-CARD of the PW 1 and the deceased is of Nand Nagri, Delhi which was 20.11.2005.
Therefore, it can be said that the petitioners are the resident of Delhi.
Therefore, Therefore, no doubt is left to the mind of the court that the petitioner has been the residents of Delhi.

16. Somwati and Ors. that wife and other claimants are entitled for Loss of Consortium whether it is wife or son or daughter.

Parental consortium: a parents' society, affection and companionship given to a child.
Spousal consortium: A spouses' society, affection and companionship given to the other spouse.

As far as the head of Loss of Dependency is concerned, same is to be calculated as per the multiplier method which has been adopted as a thumb rule in Sarla Verma vs. DTC [2009 (6) Scale 129] and various other judgments, unless there are exceptional circumstances which make it necessary to depart from the said rule.

Further, in the judgment titled as National Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra) it has been concluded by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that in determination of the multiplicand the deduction for personal and living expenses the Tribunals shall be guided by the law as laid in Sarla Verma's case.

Therefore, this Tribunal has no option but to take the minimum wages of an 'post graduate and above' as applicable in Delhi.
The accident took place on 22.08.2019 and the minimum wages for "post graduate and above" person as on the date of accident were Rs. 19,060/- per month applicable in Delhi.

Therefore, one-fourth is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

After deduction, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.
20,013/-.
Thus, the loss of dependency comes to Rs. 36,02,340/- (Rs. 20,013/- x 12 x 15).
I therefore, award Rs. 36,02,340/- to the petitioners towards loss of dependency.

opennyai_summary.facts:
He submitted that at the time of accident driver Bablu was driving the vehicle bearing UP-14-HT- 2967 in control speed.
He submitted that the vehicle was duly insured.

His children are not doing any job.
9. Respondents have not examined any witness in their defence.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether deceased Kavita Gupta succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road accident on 22.08.2019 at 2.05 pm opposite Sai Hotel G.T. Road due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. UP-14-HT-2963 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent Neeraj Aggarwal and ors.
2. To what amount of compensation the LRs of the deceased are entitled and from whom?
13. Now, the court has to assess as to how much compensation be awarded to the petitioners and by whom.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11.It is well settled law that where petition under Section 166 of the Act is instituted, it becomes the duty of the petitioner to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver.
In a petition under Motor Neeraj Aggarwal And Ors. vs Babluy And Ors. on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13499957/
3 Vehicles Act, Tribunal need not go into the technicality because strict rules of procedure and evidence are not followed.
Basically, in road accident cases, Tribunal has simply to quantify the compensation which is just rational and reasonable on the basis of enquiry.
Though it is an admitted legal position that the negligence on the part of driver with respect to the use of vehicle needs to be established but the same is to be established on the principles of preponderance of probabilities as decided in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Harsh Mishra & Ors. III(2015) ACC 435 Delhi.
Neeraj Aggarwal and ors. Vs Babluy and ors. 18.01.2023 Page No. 5 of 18 12.
In the present case, manner of accident has not been disputed.
First of all the court has to decide as to whom the liability to pay the compensation is fastened.
14.As regards the liability, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, therefore primary liability to compensate the petitioner is that of respondent no.1.
As the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no.2, so, it is vicariously liable to compensate the petitioner.
It is an admitted position on record that the offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident.
Therefore, it is the respondent no. 3 who has to compensate the petitioner being the insurer.
16. So far so, the loss of consortium is concerned, it has been decided by the Apex Court on 07.09.2020 in Civil Appeal No. 3093/2020 arising out of SLP (C) No. 23478/2019 in case titled as The New India Assurance Company Limited Vs Smt. Somwati and Ors. that wife and other claimants are entitled for Loss of Consortium whether it is wife or son or daughter.
Filial consortium a child's society, affection and companionship given to a parent.
Spousal consortium: A spouses' society, affection and companionship given to the other spouse.
Hence, the wife, son and mother of the deceased are left behind as legal heirs.
Therefore, all the three petitioners being the wife, son, mother of the deceased are entitled to consortium.
As far as the head of Loss of Dependency is concerned, same is to be calculated as per the multiplier method which has been adopted as a thumb rule in Sarla Verma vs. DTC [2009 (6) Scale 129] and various other judgments, unless there are exceptional circumstances which make it necessary to depart from the said rule.
Further, in the judgment titled as National Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra) it has been concluded by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that in determination of the multiplicand the deduction for personal and living expenses the Tribunals shall be guided by the law as laid in Sarla Verma's case.
Hence, the applicable multiplier would be '15'.
19.
In the present case deceased was a housewife and did not have any permanent income but she had been rendering gratuitous Neeraj Aggarwal and ors. Vs Babluy and ors. 18.01.2023
However, no document has been placed on record in regard to the income and employment of the deceased.
Therefore, this Tribunal has no option but to take the minimum wages of an 'post graduate and above' as applicable in Delhi.
The accident took place on 22.08.2019 and the minimum wages for "post graduate and above" person as on the date of accident were Rs. 19,060/- per month applicable in Delhi.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Neeraj Aggarwal and ors. Vs Babluy and ors. 18.01.2023 Page No. 9 of 18 Insurance Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra) has held that future prospects have to be considered for calculating the loss of income.
opennyai_summary.decision:
the income of the deceased come to 19,060/- for the assessment of the future loss of income.
The deceased was below 50 years of age therefore, an addition of 40% as future prospects has to be made.
After adding future prospects, the income of the deceased comes to Rs. 26,684/- (Rs. 19,060/- + 19,060/- x 40/ 100).
Legal heirs i.e., petitioner no.1 to 4 can be said to be dependent upon the income of the deceased.
Therefore, one-fourth is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
After deduction, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.
20,013/-.
Thus, the loss of dependency comes to Rs. 36,02,340/- (Rs. 20,013/- x 12 x 15).
I therefore, award Rs. 36,02,340/- to the petitioners towards loss of dependency.
